name: St. Anton am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: St. Anton am Arlberg is the world-renowned cradle of alpine skiing, captivating summer visitors with the Valluga cable car, via ferratas, and Verwall valley.
beschreibung:
Overview

The legendary alpine resort of St. Anton am Arlberg lies at an elevation of 1,304 meters at the foot of the historic Arlberg Pass in the Tyrolean Oberland. Internationally hailed as the birthplace of modern alpine skiing, it is here that pioneers such as Hannes Schneider formulated the iconic Arlberg technique in the early 20th century. Today, St. Anton presents itself as a vibrant, cosmopolitan mountain haven featuring cutting-edge infrastructure alongside authentic alpine character. Flanked by the rugged limestone towers of the Lechtal Alps and the glaciated peaks of the Verwall group, the resort is a launchpad for scenic cable car rides, demanding via ferratas, and panoramic high-alpine trails. The Ski Arlberg network ranks among the five largest ski areas in the world and draws mountain enthusiasts from across the globe in every season.

Route & Requirements

The pedestrianised centre of St. Anton is entirely barrier-free and invites leisurely strolls amidst charming mountain architecture. From town, ultra-modern lifts such as the Galzigbahn with its Ferris wheel mechanism, the Gampenbahn, and the daring Vallugabahn whisk visitors up into high-alpine terrain reaching the 2,811-meter Valluga peak. Families and casual hikers will love the gentle, stroller-accessible path leading into the picturesque Verwall valley to Lake Verwallsee (approx. 1 hour, flat), featuring interactive sensory stations and a suspension bridge. Seasoned alpinists can test their skills on the challenging Arlberg Via Ferrata or the high-altitude Berggeistweg, both requiring surefootedness, complete via ferrata safety gear, and robust mountain boots. Traditional mountain huts offer inviting rest stops along the routes.

Visit & Arrival

St. Anton is a prime year-round mountain destination. The summer season runs from mid-June to early October, followed by winter from late November to late April. Summer visitors staying locally enjoy complimentary cable car rides and admissions with the St. Anton Summer Card. Accessibility is unmatched: as the highest ICE and Railjet express station in the world, St. Anton is connected directly to Europe's railway network. Drivers arrive toll-free via the B197 from the Inntal valley or over the scenic Arlberg Pass.

Tips

Visit the St. Anton Museum housed inside the historic Arlberg-Kandahar Villa to immerse yourself in the rich heritage of alpine skiing. Ascending to the top Valluga viewing platform rewards you on clear days with an awe-inspiring 360-degree panorama encompassing five countries and countless alpine peaks.
preis: Town freely accessible; cable cars require tickets (St. Anton Summer Card valid)
oeffnungszeiten: Open year-round; main operating seasons mid-June to early October and late November to late April
